title: RBAC v2 change-control and audit export playbook
content:
Purpose and scope

This is a working playbook for performing change-control, reconciliation, and SIEM-ready audit export for RBAC v2. It focuses on the migration surface between RBAC v1 (role-centric) and RBAC v2 (attribute-assisted entitlements), the evidence automation patterns we need to produce for compliance audits, and the pragmatic steps SRE/Security/Product take during rollout windows.

This doc is intentionally operational — expect TODOs, quick commands, and checklists. Not a final policy: that will live in Confluence (linked above) once we sign off.

High-level strategy

- Keep policy evaluation deterministic and observable: every decision must produce a decision-id and an evidence bundle (policy-version, inputs, evaluation-path).
- Preserve backwards compatibility: provide a compatibility shim for v1 role checks to call into v2 policy engine until we finish cutover.
- Export strong telemetry to SIEM at multiple levels: decision-level events, change-control events (grant/revoke/request), and periodic reconciliation summaries.
- Automate as much evidence collection as possible to reduce manual auditor effort.

Key actors and responsibilities

- Security (policy owners): define attribute-to-role mappings, compliance-ready evidence schema, acceptance criteria.
- Platform/Serving Runtime: implement decision hooks, attach decision-id to request traces, enforce rate-limited audit forwarders.
- Release/SRE: risk windows, canary cohorts, rollbacks, capacity for increased audit traffic.
- Product/CS: communicate breaking changes to customers and manage entitlement migration.

Decision/evidence schema (operational summary)

We need a compact, SIEM-friendly JSON lines schema that fits existing ingestion pipelines. Minimal required fields:
- event_timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_type (decision | grant | revoke | reconciliation | change_control)
- principal_id
- principal_attributes (flattened key=value pairs, see mapping below)
- resource_id
- action (read/write/admin/other)
- policy_id
- policy_version
- decision (allow | deny | conditional)
- decision_id (UUID)
- inputs_hash (sha256 of normalized inputs)
- evidence_refs (list of artifact ids / S3 keys / DB ids)
- operator (who triggered change, optional)
- correlation_id (request-level trace id)

Notes: keep principal_attributes flattened to avoid nested objects — SIEM indexing performs better. We will supply a helper normalizer in the SDKs to produce "attr.email=...", "attr.team=..." pairs.

Reconciliation model and frequency

- Scope: user grants that give access to production resources and any service account with owner-like permissions.
- Delta detection: nightly reconciliation job per tenancy that compares authoritative backing store (rbac-core postgres) against live effective permissions (fast path queries against evaluation engine cache).
- Outcomes: matched, stale-grant, unexpected-grant, missing-grant. Each outcome produces an event exported to SIEM and a ticket (JIRA) for owners when remediation required.
- Retention: reconciliation snapshots stored for 180 days in compliance bucket.

Change-control workflow (high level)

1) Request phase: change requested via UI/API -> creates change-control record in rbac-control service.
2) Pre-validate: lint policy, run dry-run evaluation across sampled requests, produce impact report (list of principals/resources affected).
3) Approvals: automated approvals for low-risk changes (e.g., attribute label mapping) vs. human approvals for high-impact (owner scope).
4) Staged apply: canary cohort 1 (1% of requests) -> expand to 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Each stage emits change-control events and daily reconciliation.
5) Post-apply audit: generate evidence bundle and attach to the change record.

Rollout phases and gating

- Phase 0: Instrumentation only (no enforcement changes). Emit decision events for every request; set policy evaluation mode to "observe". Duration: 2–4 weeks depending on traffic.
- Phase 1: Dual-eval + shim (enforce v1 default but log v2 decisions). Canary 1% for 48h.
- Phase 2: Partial enforcement on low-risk resources. Canary expand 10% then 50%.
- Phase 3: Full enforcement for non-critical environments (staging).
- Phase 4: Full enforcement production with fallback policies and automated rollback triggers.

Rollout gates (examples)

- Error budget: decision engine error rate < 0.5% during canary window.
- Latency: 95th percentile decision latency < 15ms additional over baseline.
- False-deny rate (compared to v1 baseline) < 0.1% after 48h.
- Evidence completeness: 100% of decisions have decision_id and at least one evidence_ref.

Operational runbook snippets (copy/paste)

- Force export of last 24h decisions for tenant X (SQL-like pseudo):
  SELECT * FROM decision_events WHERE tenant_id = 'tenant-X' AND event_timestamp >= now() - interval '24 hours';

- Generate impact report for change Y: 
  ./tools/impact-run --change-id=Y --sample=10000 --out=reports/Y-impact.json

- Reconcile stale grants for service-account Z (one-off):
  POST /reconcile/run {"scope":"service-account","id":"Z"} -> returns ticket id JIRA-...

SIEM mapping and transform notes

- We will ship a lightweight forwarder that performs two transforms: flatten attributes and map Redwood schema to SIEM canonical fields (host, source_user, event_type, etc.).
- Normalization rules: principal_id -> source_user.id, event_type -> event.action_type, decision -> event.outcome.
- Sensitive fields: never forward raw principal_attributes.email to third-party SIEM unless the tenant has explicitly consented. Instead forward pseudonymized principal_id and attr.team.

Evidence automation patterns

- Evidence bundles should be assembled at decision-time when feasible: store policy snapshot (policy_id+version), normalized inputs, decision trace, and a low-entropy hash linking to any large artifacts (audit logs, request bodies).
- For change-control records, collect: reviewer list, approver signatures, dry-run impact report, canary metrics, and reconciliation snapshot. Attach S3 URIs to evidence_refs.

Migration checklist (practical)

- [ ] Instrumentation implemented in serving-runtime (decision hook + decision_id tag).
- [ ] Forwarder deployed to dev and staging SIEM ingestion.
- [ ] Reconciliation job implemented and scheduled in airflow.
- [ ] Change-control UI integrated with approver workflow.
- [ ] SDK helpers published for attribute flattening and inputs normalization.
- [ ] Data retention policy configured for reconciliation snapshots (180d).
- [ ] Privacy review completed for email and PII forwarding.

Open questions / TODOs

- How do we best represent conditional decisions (e.g., allow-if-justification) in the minimal SIEM schema? Proposal: decision=conditional + condition_code and condition_expires_at.
- Do we require cryptographic signing for evidence bundles in v1? Compliance wants strong provenance; product is concerned about operational weight.
- Investigate cost impact of exporting full decision stream for the largest tenants. Maybe sample at 1% and request full export on-demand for audits.

Appendix: example export line (single-line JSON)

{"event_timestamp":"2025-01-31T21:12:03Z","event_type":"decision","principal_id":"user:U-12345","principal_attributes":"attr.team=payments,attr.env=prod","resource_id":"dataset:PAYMENTS-TRANS","action":"read","policy_id":"rbac-v2/allow-payments-read","policy_version":"2025-01-17-3","decision":"allow","decision_id":"9f8b7e2a-3c3f-4b6a-8a2b-0e7d1c5c2a11","inputs_hash":"sha256:abcd...","evidence_refs":"s3://redwood-evidence/decisions/9f8b7e2a.json","correlation_id":"trace-7a8b9c"}

Contacts and communication

- Slack channel: #sec-rbac-migration (use for urgent canary failures)
- Pager on-call: sec-oncall (for production decision-engine incidents)
- Owners: Priya Narang (policy), Ethan Morales (runtime), Marta Kowalski (reconciliation)

If you're reading this and think we missed a pragmatic step, add a comment inline or file JIRA-SEC-2001 (migration checklist) and tag @Priya.
